amendments.because: A fixed size and every round's own summary forever cannot both hold; the owner's goal is never hitting the limit
amendments.done_when: The pull request keeps per-round time summaries rather than every event, so a long item never reaches the body limit and keeps its whole round history

done_when: The pull request time record has a fixed size limit: it keeps a time summary for each of the recent rounds and folds older rounds into one totals line, so a long item never reaches the body limit and the board still shows its total time

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 4
Raise: Not done
`_compact` retains every row from the latest worker round. Forge records progress as often as every ten seconds (`src/forge/repo.py:304–326`), so a single long worker round can put hundreds of progress rows into the pull request record without triggering a fold. Once the body budget is exceeded, `_bounded_body` deletes event and timing rows (`src/forge/close.py:914–923`), which can remove evidence needed for that recent round's time summary. This newly identified current-round path remains after the earlier finding about older rounds was settled.
findings.title: Not done: Current-round progress leaves the time record unbounded

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
The proof copies short rounds into 200 earlier reviews, including the repeated-close case, but never grows progress records within the current worker round. It can pass while the current-round record exceeds the body budget and `_bounded_body` removes time evidence. The other named proofs do not cover that long single-round path.

stop.reason: Owner chose one more round: fold by the number of records, not by building round, so repeated closes in one round also fold; the test adds many reviews in one round and checks each recent line has its time summary.

why: A long item's pull request time record grows toward GitHub's 64 KB body limit, and Forge trims older time detail from about round 16
